{
  "research_question": "Does the mouse navigation stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, or Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "For 'Success', since the dependent variable is binary (0/1) based on the range [0.0, 1.0], a standard ANOVA may be inappropriate; consider a Chi-Square Test of Independence or Logistic Regression as a primary alternative, though ANOVA can be used as an approximation if proportions are balanced.",
    "For 'Path Efficiency', check for extreme skewness given the range [0.0009, 29.82] which spans nearly three orders of magnitude; if normality is violated, apply a log transformation before ANOVA.",
    "For the other variables (Time-to-Target, Average Speed, AD), proceed with standard one-way ANOVA if normality and homoscedasticity assumptions are met.",
    "Calculate the F-statistic and p-value for each model to determine if the omnibus null hypothesis (all group means are equal) can be rejected."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Verify that residuals for each response variable are approximately normally distributed using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests within each paradigm group.",
    "Homogeneity of Variances: Test for equal variances across the five paradigm groups using Levene's Test or Bartlett's Test.",
    "Independence: Confirm that mouse subjects are independent (checked by 'Mouse' column having 8 levels) and trials are randomly assigned or balanced.",
    "Outliers: Inspect boxplots for extreme values, particularly in 'Path Efficiency' and 'Time-to-Target' which have high maximum values relative to means.",
    "Linearity: Not strictly required for one-way ANOVA but relevant if interactions were added later."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any ANOVA yields a p-value < 0.05, conduct post-hoc pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "Report mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for each pair of paradigms.",
    "For 'Success', if ANOVA is deemed inappropriate, perform a Chi-Square test followed by pairwise comparison of proportions with Bonferroni correction.",
    "If variances are significantly unequal (violating homogeneity), use Welch's ANOVA followed by Games-Howell post-hoc tests."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Time-to-Target and Average Speed are expected to differ significantly between paradigms, likely showing faster performance in 'ICMS Only' or 'Combined' compared to 'Sham' or single-modality visual conditions.",
    "Success rates may vary, with 'Combined' or 'ICMS Only' potentially yielding higher success probabilities than 'Dim Visual Only' or 'Sham'.",
    "Path Efficiency is expected to show significant differences, with multimodal stimulation ('Combined') potentially offering more direct paths than unimodal or sham conditions.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is expected to decrease (less dispersion) in effective stimulation conditions compared to Sham or single-modality conditions.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm likely acts as a control or baseline showing high performance, while 'Sham' and specific single-modality conditions may show deficits."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Unbalanced sample sizes across paradigms (e.g., Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505) may reduce power for detecting differences in smaller groups and violate ANOVA assumptions regarding robustness if variance is also unequal.",
    "Potential violation of normality assumptions due to the skewed distribution of 'Time-to-Target' and 'Path Efficiency' (large max values relative to means).",
    "The variable 'Success' is binary; treating it as a continuous metric in ANOVA is statistically suboptimal.",
    "Single experiment run (Replication: 1) limits the ability to generalize findings or assess consistency across experimental sessions.",
    "The 'Mouse' factor is ignored in the primary ANOVA plan, assuming no significant inter-individual variability, which could mask true effects if specific mice perform poorly regardless of paradigm."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a General Linear Model (GLM) or Mixed-Effects ANOVA including 'Mouse' as a random effect to account for subject variability, and apply log-transformation to skewed continuous variables before analysis."
}
